brief.headline: The front end discounted prompt metal for a second straight day and the inventory draw stayed switched off - the exact bearish test set yesterday, failed on both limbs - while Chinese physical buyers quietly went the other way and started restocking into the fall.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: THE PRICE FELL AGAIN AND THE CURVE LOOSENED FURTHER. The 19-August official cash settlement was $3,191.50, down $27.50 (-0.85%), and the three-month was $3,212.00, down $22.00 (-0.68%). Because the prompt fell harder than the forward for a second consecutive session, the cash-3M discount WIDENED from $15.00 to $20.50 - the widest prompt discount on the published board since late February. Exchange inventory was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes for a second consecutive session, so the run of 34 daily declines that ended on 18-August has not restarted.

WHY IT MATTERS: THIS WAS A PUBLISHED TEST, NOT A RETROSPECTIVE RATIONALISATION. Yesterday's read set the bar in advance: a return to a flat or firmer front end would have marked 18-August as a one-day artefact, whereas a second consecutive discount or a stock build would confirm that the seven-week drawdown was never really about prompt scarcity. The second consecutive discount printed and it printed wider, with the stock line flat rather than drawing. For seven weeks two independent series - falling inventory and a firm front end - argued the same tight-market case; they have now stopped arguing it together.

THE CURRENCY MAKES IT A CLEANER SIGNAL, NOT A MUDDIER ONE. On 18-August the metal fell while the dollar was flat. On 19-August the dollar actually WEAKENED - the exchange's own EUR/USD fixing rose to 1.16030 from 1.15770 and the dollar index is marked at 98.891, down 0.77% - and the metal fell anyway. When a dollar-priced commodity declines into a softening dollar, the move is in the commodity's own supply and demand rather than in the unit it is quoted in.

WHAT TO WATCH: THE PAPER MARKET AND THE PHYSICAL MARKET ARE NOW POINTING DIFFERENT WAYS ON THE SAME DAY. A 20-August Chinese spot review describes futures extending their decline while regional spot stayed stable to firm - holders withholding cargo, discounts and concessions almost disappearing, quotations moving to a small premium, circulating volume tightening and downstream buyers stepping up restocking into the low price. That is the first dated evidence in over a week running AGAINST the demand-weakness case, and it is one session against a two-session curve signal. Which of the two persists into next week is the question that decides whether this is a correction inside an uptrend or the start of a surplus structure.

The three-month settled $3,212.00, down $22.00 (-0.68%). Cash fell MORE than the three-month for a second consecutive session, so the cash-3M spread WIDENED from a $15.00 CONTANGO to a $20.50 CONTANGO - the widest prompt discount on this published board since 27-February. AND THE INVENTORY LINE STAYED FLAT FOR A SECOND SESSION: LME aluminium stock was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes, a reported daily change of exactly ZERO, so the run of 34 consecutive daily declines that ended on 18-August has not restarted. YESTERDAY THIS DASHBOARD SET A BINARY TEST AND PUBLISHED IT IN ADVANCE: 'a return to a flat or backwardated spread today would mark 18-August as a one-day artefact; a SECOND CONSECUTIVE CONTANGO, or an outright stock BUILD after yesterday's flat print, would confirm that the seven-week drawdown was never about prompt scarcity and would be the most bearish structural sequence this board has produced.' The second consecutive contango printed, and it printed WIDER. The one-day-artefact reading is now closed off by the market's own settlement. THE DOLLAR MAKES IT WORSE, NOT BETTER. On 18-August the metal fell while the dollar was flat, so none of the decline was currency. On 19-August the dollar WEAKENED - the LME EUR/USD fixing rose to 1.16030 from 1.15770 and Trading Economics marks DXY at 98.891, down 0.77% - and the metal fell anyway. A dollar-denominated commodity that declines into a weakening dollar is being sold on its own fundamentals, and that is a harder read than a flat-dollar decline. THE GIVE-BACK FROM THE 11-AUGUST HIGH OF $3,373.00 IS NOW $181.50 (-5.38%) IN SIX SESSIONS, and the market holds just $32.00 (+1.01%) above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50 - the level carried here as the explicit technical invalidation. THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT, REPORTED RATHER THAN BURIED, AND IT IS DATED TODAY: SMM's 20-August South China spot review describes the Chinese physical market moving in the OPPOSITE direction to the exchange curve - futures extending their decline while spot stayed stable to firm, cargo holders withholding, price cuts and concessions almost disappearing, mainstream quotations at a premium of 0 to +10 yuan/mt with the centre moving upward, liquidity noticeably tightening and downstream buyers ramping up restocking into the low price. Paper and physical are pointing different ways on the same day, and that divergence is the single most important thing to watch from here.

kpis.label: LME 3-Month
kpis.note: The 19-August official three-month settled $3,212.00, DOWN $22.00 (-0.68%) from $3,234.00. It sits $20.50 ABOVE cash, which is a CONTANGO by the convention stated on this board: cash below three-month. The forward has now fallen less than the prompt on two consecutive sessions, which is the arithmetic that widened the discount. Year-to-date the three-month is +6.69% against the first-published 2026 official of $3,010.50 on 02-January. Read against the 11-August cycle high of $3,374.00 on the same tenor, the forward has surrendered $162.00 (-4.80%) in six sessions - slightly less than cash has given back, which is precisely why the curve has loosened at the front rather than shifted down in parallel. A parallel shift would be a price story; a front-end loosening is a structure story, and structure is what regional premium negotiations are argued on.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: MINUS $20.50 - A CONTANGO, AND THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE ONE. Cash $3,191.50 settled $20.50 BELOW the three-month of $3,212.00, widening from the $15.00 contango printed on 18-August, which had itself crossed from exactly $0.00 on 17-August. CONVENTION, STATED EVERY RUN SO IT CANNOT BE MISREAD: cash ABOVE three-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt scarcity; cash BELOW three-month is CONTANGO and signals the market will not pay for prompt metal. THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE ARE MOVING IN THE SAME DIRECTION, WHICH IS THE ORDINARY CASE AND IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY BECAUSE THE OPPOSITE HAPPENED EARLIER THIS CYCLE: both fell, so there is no divergence to reconcile and no benign reading available. This is the widest prompt discount on the published board since 27-February. THE STRUCTURAL POINT: for seven weeks the bull case rested on a drawing inventory and a firm front end saying the same thing. Those two series have now stopped saying it together - inventory has been flat for two sessions and the front end has discounted prompt metal for two sessions. A market that is genuinely short of prompt units does not do both at once.

THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE MOVED IN THE SAME DIRECTION, which is the ordinary case and is worth saying plainly precisely because the opposite happened repeatedly earlier in this cycle: there is no divergence to reconcile here and no benign reading available. AND THE INVENTORY LINE STAYED SWITCHED OFF. LME aluminium warrant was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes, a reported daily change of exactly ZERO, for a second consecutive session. The run of 34 consecutive daily declines that ended on 18-August has not restarted. SMM's independent flash note records LME aluminium inventory at 246,900 mt on 19-August, unchanged day on day, down 4,775 t (-1.90%) on the week and down 32,900 t (-11.74%) on the month. Two flat sessions is no longer attributable to one day's warranting mechanics. THIS WAS A PUBLISHED TEST AND IT WAS FAILED ON BOTH LIMBS. Yesterday's catalyst read set the bar in advance: a return to a flat or backwardated spread would have marked 18-August as a one-day artefact of a complex-wide repricing, whereas a second consecutive contango or an outright stock build would confirm that the seven-week drawdown was never about prompt scarcity. The second consecutive contango printed, and it printed wider. THE CURRENCY MAKES THE SIGNAL CLEANER, NOT MUDDIER, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ANALYTICAL POINT OF THE RUN. On 18-August the metal fell while the dollar was flat, so the decline could be attributed to the metal only weakly. On 19-August the dollar WEAKENED MATERIALLY - the LME's own EUR/USD fixing rose to 1.16030 from 1.15770, the ECB fixing to 1.16050 from 1.15760 and BFIX to 1.16034 from 1.15756, all three rolling together, with Trading Economics marking DXY at 98.891, down 0.77%, and the US 10-year easing to 4.659% - and the metal fell anyway. A dollar-priced commodity that declines into a softening dollar and falling nominal yields is being sold on its own balance. The currency was working in the metal's favour and lost. THE COMPLEX AGREES. Four of the five metals on this board fell on their three-month officials - aluminium -0.68%, copper -1.35%, zinc -1.93%, lead -1.00%, nickel -0.21% - and three posted large inventory builds: copper +12,425 t to 235,975, lead +9,575 t to 418,575, zinc +8,525 t to 95,050. Copper's two-session build now totals 28,150 tonnes, a 13.55% increase in its visible stock in forty-eight hours. THE GIVE-BACK NOW STANDS AT $181.50 (-5.38%) FROM THE 11-AUGUST HIGH OF $3,373.00 IN SIX SESSIONS, and cash holds just $32.00 (+1.01%) above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50, the level this dashboard carries as its explicit technical invalidation. THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT IS DATED TODAY AND IT IS GENUINE. SMM's 20-August South China spot review describes the Chinese physical market moving in the opposite direction to the exchange curve: futures extending their decline while spot stayed stable to firm, the cumulative price fall having clearly broken below the monthly average, cargo holders withholding, price cuts and concessions almost disappearing, mainstream quotations at a 0 to +10 yuan/mt premium with the centre rising, liquidity noticeably tightening, and downstream buyers ramping up restocking into the low price - with traders unable to source cheap lots and ending up absorbing cargo at flat prices. SHFE warrants also fell a further 2,393 mt to 290,536 mt, down 22.33% on the month against the LME's 11.74%. Paper and physical are pointing different ways on the same day. That tension is the single most important thing to watch from here, and it will not stay unresolved for long.

NO PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRICE PRINT DATED AFTER 07-AUGUST HAS BEEN FOUND AT THIS COMPILE, SO NO VALUE ON THIS PANEL IS CHANGED FOR A NINTH CONSECUTIVE RUN - the events are recorded, the price is not invented. A dedicated search on 20-Aug-2026 again returned only the 05-August FOB East Australia transaction and the 07-August CIF Malaysia transaction. Nine runs without a public seaborne print is itself the finding, and it is reported rather than papered over. THE SUPPLY EVENT RESOLVED AND HAS STAYED RESOLVED FOR A SEVENTH RUN. Norsk Hydro announced on 13-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - is ramping back to FULL capacity after Brazil's regulator ANP approved it as a self-importer of natural gas and a temporary terminal-access agreement was reached with gas supplier CELBA. The disruption ran three days from the 11-August disclosure of a cut to 50%. Lost production is put at 100,000-120,000 tonnes with a guided potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million. THE HONEST READ IS UNCHANGED: the cost consequence was never observed, because the outage never lasted long enough to produce a public seaborne price print and now almost certainly never will. THE OTHER RECENT PRINT, STATED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE BASIS DIFFERS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-Aug-2026. CIF Malaysia is a delivered price including freight; FOB East Australia is a load-port price, so the $9/mt gap is broadly freight rather than a rally. MARGIN CONTEXT AT A LOWER METAL PRICE, AND IT MOVED THE WRONG WAY AGAIN TODAY: against the 19-August three-month official of $3,212.00 the FOB mark now sits at about 11.1% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 11.4%, both slightly HIGHER as ratios than yesterday purely because the metal fell $22.00 while the alumina marks did not move. Both remain well below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%, so the alumina leg is still a clear TAILWIND to smelter economics - but the ratio is now being driven by the numerator's denominator, which is a polite way of saying the tailwind shrinks every time the metal falls.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided hot metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter currently at about 18% of capacity. THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments. THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

Press Metal Aluminium reported net profit of MYR 624.5m for the quarter ended 31-March-2026, UP 35.2% year-on-year from MYR 461.77m, on revenue of MYR 4.1bn (+5.2%). A 35% profit increase at a producer with no exposure to either strongly supports the former. status.impact: UPDATED THIS RUN WITH NEW PUBLIC DETAIL AND A NEW CHARACTERISATION. SMM's 16-August weekly review gives the DENOMINATOR for the first time: 18% of the plant's 1,262 pots have been restarted following the 28-March attack - roughly 227 pots - with production expected to recover to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027. Crucially SMM states that the pace of resumption has been FASTER THAN THE MARKET PREVIOUSLY EXPECTED and concludes that the supply tightness premium priced in earlier now faces giveback pressure, with upside room capped to some extent by resumption expectations. The 12-August H1 release had already put roughly US$400m of recovery capital behind it, with H1 aluminium sales down 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production down 29% to 1.01 Mt. NEW ALUMINA DETAIL: the associated refinery's H1-2026 production fell significantly year-on-year and its capacity recovered to 50% of pre-incident levels in early July. Still the largest single supply loss in the market, but the recovery now has both a published end date and a published run-rate that is beating expectations.

status.impact: A CLOSURE RISK OVER UP TO 590,000 t/y - ALMOST 40% OF AUSTRALIAN PRODUCTION - HAS BEEN REMOVED. Tomago will enter a ten-year power purchase agreement after its existing contract expires on 31-Dec-2028, taking supply to 2038 and to fully renewable electricity from 2033, and will invest A$1.1bn in real terms through 2038 including A$100m for decarbonisation, cutting Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 7.1 Mt/y from 2033. Bearish for price, structurally significant for the western smelter fleet - and the fact that a smelter this size needed public support to contract power is the most honest public statement available about western smelter economics.

status.status: At the 45 Mt policy ceiling; H1 primary production +2.2% while Citi's end-use tracker fell 0.4% y/y - the surplus is being exported as semis and alloy rather than ingot
status.impact: REFRESHED ON THE 16-AUGUST SMM WEEKLY. China's weekly aluminium production was basically stable over the past week and the proportion of liquid aluminium rose 0.11 percentage point week-on-week - a marginal shift toward direct-to-casthouse delivery rather than ingot. On the demand side the same review places the downstream processing industry in its traditional consumption off-season with operating rates under pressure, and flags that aluminium billet processing fees pulled back, weakening replacement demand for aluminium ingot - the mechanism that could slow the destocking SMM itself expects to continue but decelerate in the second half of the month.
status.update: REFRESHED ON AL CIRCLE'S 18-AUGUST TRADE ANALYSIS AND THE NEW DETAIL IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ADDITION TO THIS PANEL THIS WEEK. China's primary aluminium production rose 2.2% in the first half with smelters operating close to or slightly above the 45 Mt policy cap, while Citi's China end-use demand tracker FELL 0.4% year on year on weakness in traditional sectors, particularly construction. A production increase against a demand decrease produces exportable surplus, and the export data shows exactly where it went: semi-finished exports of 3.2 million tonnes in January-June, up 18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 tonnes; alloy exports nearly doubling to 238,500 tonnes with China turning NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019; and primary exports up 32% to 38,400 tonnes, much of which the article attributes to Western-origin metal held in Chinese bonded warehouses being redirected rather than to Chinese production leaving. THE TAX STRUCTURE IS THE MECHANISM AND IT IS PUBLIC: primary aluminium exports face a 30% tax while alloy and semis export at a zero rate, so the surplus leaves in processed form. SHFE inventories were put at 422,097 tonnes against LME inventory of 358,000 tonnes including off-warrant stocks. On the demand side, SMM's 18-August scrap review describes cast aluminium alloy operating rates continuing to decline through the high-temperature holidays and the consumption off-season with order volumes shrinking.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE AND ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CHURNED DAILY. THIS RUN CARRIES A GENUINE MATERIAL CHANGE AND THE PANEL IS UPDATED ACCORDINGLY, WHICH IS WHY THE AS-OF DATE MOVED. AL Circle published a detailed analysis on 18-August quantifying how China is filling the Western supply gap created by the Gulf losses, and the composition of that flow is a corridor fact rather than a price fact: semi-finished aluminium exports of 3.2 million tonnes in January-June, up 18% year on year, with June shipments of 695,000 tonnes a monthly record; alloy exports nearly doubling to 238,500 tonnes, with China becoming a NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019; and primary exports up 32% to 38,400 tonnes, much of which is attributed to Western-origin metal held in Chinese bonded warehouses being redirected rather than to Chinese production leaving the country - Chinese data recorded 9,700 tonnes exported to the United States in January-June against US customs data recording only 70 tonnes of Chinese imports. The tax structure is the mechanism: primary aluminium exports face a 30% tax while alloy and semis export at a zero rate, and Beijing removed the 13% VAT export rebate on aluminium products in December 2024, which cut semis exports 18% to 890,000 tonnes last year before the Gulf disruption revived them. THE SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE IS EXPLICITLY FLAGGED IN THE SOURCE AND BELONGS ON A TRADE PANEL: when Western buyers import Chinese bars, rods and tubes instead of raw metal for local conversion, fabrication activity relocates, which is why Western policymakers have imposed anti-dumping duties on Chinese aluminium products. THE REST OF THE CORRIDOR PICTURE IS UNCHANGED AND WAS RE-VERIFIED: the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed on day 171 with no development dated after the 16-August restatement, and Trading Economics headlines both crude benchmarks as extending gains on the US-Iran stalemate; Red Sea routing around the Cape of Good Hope continues, adding roughly 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages; and Section 232 was re-verified this run at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, with the US-content relief threshold cut from 95% to 85% in June-2026 and Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU.  REVIEW NOTE (20-Aug-2026): this panel is reviewed monthly or on material change rather than churned daily. ONE POTENTIALLY MATERIAL CHANGE IS NOW IN PROGRESS AND IS FLAGGED HERE WITHOUT ALTERING ANY CORRIDOR: the United States and Canada are reported to be close to a trade agreement that would lower tariffs on steel and aluminium and introduce an export quota, with a planned 50% tariff on additional Canadian goods postponed by three days. If a deal concludes, the North American corridor and the US duty-paid premium decomposition will both need revisiting. Nothing has been changed yet, because nothing has been signed. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed on day 172 with no public change in the position.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, AND THE TEST IS AGAIN BINARY AND CHEAP TO SCORE. THE QUESTION IS WHETHER TWO SESSIONS OF CONTANGO BECOME THREE. A return to a flat or backwardated spread today would frame the last two sessions as a corrective episode inside an intact uptrend, consistent with a complex-wide repricing in which four of five metals loosened. A THIRD CONSECUTIVE CONTANGO - especially alongside an outright stock BUILD after two flat prints - would establish a front-end REGIME rather than an episode, and would be the most bearish structural sequence this board has produced. SECOND, THE LEVELS. Cash at $3,191.50 sits $32.00 above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50, the explicit invalidation carried on this board; a close beneath it takes the correction deeper than a simple second wave allows and opens $3,105 and then $3,061.50. WHETHER THE REPORTED CLAIM THAT EX-CHINA LME ALUMINIUM STOCK IS OVERWHELMINGLY RUSSIAN-ORIGIN IS CORROBORATED OR CONTESTED. This remains the highest-value undated item on the board and its value has RISEN this run, because it is the single hypothesis that reconciles the two contradictory signals now on this page. If ex-China LME warrant is largely material Western buyers cannot use, then a flat LME inventory line and a loosening LME front end can coexist with genuinely tightening regional physical markets - exactly the pattern observed on 19 and 20-August. If the claim is wrong, the exchange curve is the leading indicator and the Chinese physical firmness is noise. The claim is attributed to a named analyst in trade press and is a single-source analytical statement at this compile, reported as such and not as an exchange statistic. The LME publishes country-of-origin warrant data periodically; corroboration or contradiction from that primary source, or from a second research house, is what would move this from a strong hypothesis to a fact.

The most recent public restatement remains the 16-August review in which the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the Strait will remain closed unless the United States changes its behaviour, with reopening conditional on five stated conditions including a permanent halt to military operations; the US President is separately reported as preferring economic pressure to another large-scale military operation, and Iran's Foreign Minister says there are no negotiations under way though mediators continue trying. THE MARKET-SIDE CORROBORATION IS AGAIN IN CRUDE RATHER THAN METALS AND IT STRENGTHENED - Brent extended to $92.38, up 1.50% on the day and up 4.4% across two compiles, on a vendor narrative of US-Iran stalemate. The energy complex has now priced the stalemate higher on two consecutive sessions while the metals complex sold off on both, which argues the metal's decline owes nothing to any improvement in the geopolitical picture.

PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL. TREND MOVED FROM UP TO FLAT THIS RUN, AND THE CHANGE IS EVIDENCE-DRIVEN AND DELIBERATE. For over a week the demand evidence ran one way: a China end-use tracker down 0.4% year on year in H1 on construction weakness, July passenger vehicle retail down 20.9% year on year, billet processing fees below average production cost, cast alloy operating rates declining through the off-season, US July retail sales down 0.6% month on month with the core control group at its worst since January 2025. NONE OF THAT IS WITHDRAWN AND IT IS NOT BEING DOWNPLAYED. But the 20-August Chinese spot review is the first dated evidence in more than a week pointing the other way, and it is specific rather than atmospheric: cargo holders withholding, price cuts and concessions almost disappearing, mainstream quotations moving to a 0 to +10 yuan/mt premium with the centre steadily rising, liquidity noticeably tightening, downstream buyers ramping up restocking because the absolute price had broken below the monthly average, and traders attempting to push prices lower unable to source cheap lots and ultimately absorbing cargo at flat prices and accepting small premiums. Spot transactions centred on the SHFE 2609 contract at a premium of 75 to 115 yuan/mt. ONE SESSION DOES NOT OVERTURN A QUARTER OF DATA, WHICH IS WHY THE TREND MOVES TO FLAT RATHER THAN DOWN. If the same pattern is reported for a third and fourth session, this row goes to down.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. TREND REMAINS UP AND THE CONFIGURATION HAS DETERIORATED FURTHER. The 17-August rally was expressed entirely in forward tenors, taking the cash-3M spread to zero; cash has now fallen harder than the forward on two consecutive sessions and pushed the spread to a $20.50 contango. A long expressed in the forward curve while the prompt date goes bidless is precisely the configuration that unwinds fastest when a supply schedule delivers. The price has surrendered $181.50 of a $312.50 advance in six sessions and the explicit invalidation at $3,159.50 is now only $32.00 away, which compresses the distance between an orderly correction and a forced one. AGAINST THE RISK, AND STATED FAIRLY: residual exposure is materially lower than it was at $3,374.00 precisely because so much has already been given back, and the last public observation on positioning - that in the 14-August LME session volume pulled back while open interest INCREASED, which is bulls adding rather than length liquidating - is now six sessions old and has not been refreshed. An unrefreshed observation is not evidence for today.

AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. TREND DOWN, AND THE CASE FOR DOWN STRENGTHENED FOR A NINTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. The Alunorte gas disruption - the only credible alumina cost threat of the year - resolved in three days via regulatory self-import approval and a temporary terminal-access agreement, with lost production of 100,000-120,000 t against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market and no public seaborne price print produced at any point. Nine consecutive runs have now produced no public seaborne alumina print dated after 07-August, which is itself the finding. The Gulf producer's alumina refinery separately recovered to 50% of pre-incident capacity in early July, so supply is being restored from two directions. THE ONE THING THAT MOVED THIS RUN IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN ALUMINA: against the 19-August three-month of $3,212.00 the carried FOB East Australia mark of $356/t is about 11.1% of the metal price, up from 11.0% yesterday and 10.9% the day before - three consecutive increases driven entirely by the metal falling. Against a decade rule of thumb of 15-17% alumina remains a clear tailwind, but a margin built on a favourable ratio erodes automatically as the metal declines. THE RESIDUAL RISK IS THE WORD 'TEMPORARY' IN THE TERMINAL-ACCESS AGREEMENT, and the longer-run risk is upstream - Guinea contract negotiations, elevated ocean freight and the rainy season.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE - AND THE AUGUST SETTLEMENT WINDOW HAS CLOSED WITH NOTHING PUBLISHED. Prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle conventionally around the 17th-18th; a dedicated search this run returned NO August print for any of the three, so all three rows are carried at their June or July cycles and none has been estimated. THE DIRECTIONAL RISK INTO THAT UNPRINTED SEPTEMBER SETTLEMENT ROSE FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE RUN ON THE CRUDE LEG: Brent marks $92.38 against $91.27 at the previous compile and $88.52 the one before, up 4.4% across two runs, with the vendor attributing the gain to the US-Iran stalemate, and green petroleum coke is a refinery by-product whose price follows crude with a lag. THE POWER LEG WENT THE OTHER WAY AND IS REPORTED AS SUCH: European gas TTF marks EUR 63.42/MWh, DOWN 0.35% on the day after yesterday's 3.97% jump. The two energy legs diverged today rather than reinforcing each other, which is why this row stays at Medium impact. The fluoride lines have ALREADY moved, with cryolite quotations at RMB 7,500-9,000/t from RMB 7,000-8,500/t and the August AlF3 tender price of the benchmark Chinese enterprise raised RMB 250/t month on month. TREND UP: the crude leg and the fluoride leg still point the same way at a moment when the metal has given back $181.50 from its high.

A US-CANADA TARIFF AGREEMENT DEFLATES THE US DUTY-PAID PREMIUM. NEW ROW THIS RUN, ADDED BECAUSE A DATED PUBLIC PROCESS WITH A THREE-DAY CLOCK NOW EXISTS. CNBC reported on 19-August, carried by SMM on 20-August, that the United States and Canada are moving closer to a trade agreement covering automobiles, steel and aluminium that would LOWER tariffs and introduce an EXPORT QUOTA, with the US President postponing a planned 50% tariff on a range of additional Canadian goods for three days on the stated basis that the parties are close, and the Canadian Prime Minister confirming substantial progress without a concluded negotiation. WHY THIS IS HIGH IMPACT AND NOT A CURIOSITY: Canada is the largest single source of primary aluminium imported into the United States, and at the verified 50% Section 232 rate on articles the tariff leg alone accounts for $1,595.75/t of the carried $2,380/t US duty-paid premium - roughly 67% of it. A negotiated rate reduction, or a quota admitting a defined volume at a lower rate, would deflate that component directly and mechanically rather than through any change in physical balance. TREND UP because the process has moved from speculation to an announced postponement with a stated deadline. NO PUBLISHED FIGURE ON THIS DASHBOARD HAS BEEN CHANGED ON THE STRENGTH OF A REPORTED NEGOTIATION - the rate is carried at the verified 50% and the decomposition is computed on it.

THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
